evidence: jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_2940.txt: signed Aug. 20, 1918; sole operative clause 'I do hereby amend the order of October 12, 1917 ... by changing Paragraph I of said order to read as follows' (adds War Industries Board representative to War Trade Board), plus a confirming clause ancillary to the amendment. P2 merged_into_parent_on_issue, TERM, 1918-08-20 fits; P2 disclosure present; mirror_transcription gap true.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_2913.txt: July 15, 1918, Labor Secretary may use 'Squares 229 and 230'. jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_2952.txt (S13, held): 'I hereby revoke and rescind the Executive Order issued July i 5, 1918, which authorized the Secretary of Labor ... to make use of certain premises hereinafter described', then names Squares 229 and 230; signed September 6, 1918. jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_2912.txt (same day) concerns Squares 685 and 634, so the revocation reaches 2913 only. no/ACT/1918-09-06 supported.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3042.txt: Ozark National Forest boundary modified under Act of June 4, 1897, excluded lands opened to homestead entry. Not a war order; B01 route to PD-NATIONAL-FOREST, open, correct.

jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_2953.txt: Sept. 12, 1918, Custodian 'authorized to sell at private sale' Lilly Busch real estate (Riverside Drive/Northern Ave., New York); no deadline, no record of the sale in held texts. B18 open with Custodian-report gap supported.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3016W.txt: Polk order under EO 3016 (July 1919) authorizing the Custodian 'to reject all bids at said sale, including the bid of said Johannes Meyer' for 225 Vigilant Mills shares and to resell. Single rejection/resale authorization, performance not held. B18 open correct; scan gap true.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3248A.txt: Mar. 20, 1920, rests on the Overman Act (May 20, 1918) 'as well as by virtue of any and all other acts of Congress conferring authority upon me in the premises'; directs Interior to adjust and pay Fuel Administration claims from named appropriations. B15X open with Overman end as candidate only is supported.

jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_2825A.txt: Mar. 28, 1918, under the Act of June 15, 1917; directs Navy to take possession of equipment on Netherlands vessels, adopts earlier takings, and directs the Shipping Board to pay 'full compensation'. Not only a delegation, so B13X open with shipping-fund cessation as candidate end; performance gap stated.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3030.txt: Jan. 25, 1919, 'The Executive Order of September 26, 1918, relating to the censorship of submarine cable, telegraph and telephone lines, is hereby amended to read as follows'; whole operative content is the amended text of EO 2967. P2 no/TERM/1919-01-25 with disclosure; scan gap true.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4544.txt: Nov. 13, 1926, Custodian authorized to sell at private sale for $30,000 three-fourths interest in 76 West 12th Street (Stamm sisters). No held performance record. B18 open correct.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4881.txt: May 9, 1928, private sale for $750,000 of 540.07 acres, Jefferson County, Ky. (von Zedtwitz) to Louisville park commissioners; the deed is 'to be filed simultaneously', which is prospective, not a record of the sale. B18 open correct.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3021.txt: Jan. 1919, Navy vessels purchased or commandeered for the war to be appraised by a board and sold to former owners or at public sale; equipment sold. Single course of action, performance not held. B21 open correct.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_2952.txt: Sept. 6, 1918, (1) revokes the July 15, 1918 order (EO 2913), a part spent on issue, and (2) authorizes 'the War Industries Board, for the purpose of erecting a temporary office building and maintaining and using the same during the present war emergency, to take possession of Squares 229 and 230'. Open (B21) is defensible. But the gaps point to 'the Housing Corporation's reports (EO 2912, 2952, 3296)', although EO 2952 takes the squares away from the Labor Secretary's housing program and gives them to the War Industries Board; and they omit the order's own limit 'during the present war emergency' (cf. the doctrine's EO 2652 'duration of the war' treatment) and the War Industries Board's dissolution by EO 3019-A (Jan. 1, 1919, with winding-up continuation; held S12) as disclosed candidate ends.
correct_lead: open (B21), with gaps: its own term 'during the present war emergency' and EO 3019-A's dissolution of the War Industries Board as candidate ends; War Industries Board / building records, not Housing Corporation reports, as the evidence needed; the revocation part spent on issue

evidence: jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3099.txt: 'Executive Order signed by me, dated May 12, 1919 ... be and the same hereby is amended by striking out the word "degrees" and by substituting ... jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3559A.txt: Custodian authorized to sell at private sale the one-tenth undivided interests of Carl and Elfried Bock (WPA spelling; OCR garbled) (together one-fifth) in Cleveland real estate. No performance record held. B18 open correct.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3281.txt: June 11, 1920, 'I hereby vest in the Attorney General all powers and authority conferred upon me by Section 9' of the Trading with the Enemy Act as amended (July 11, 1919; June 5, 1920). TWEA delegation; Act excepted from 1921 resolution (S1 held); no held revocation. B19 open correct.
jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3838.txt: May 9, 1923, private sale of 288 Shults Bread Co. shares (Allmers, Hildebrand) to United Bakeries; sale not recorded. B18 open correct.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3016L.txt: Polk order of April 1919 authorizing rejection of all bids (Ludwig Nisemann, $98,595) for 939 shares of K. & E. Neumond, Inc., auctioned Mar. 19, 1919, and resale. Performance not held. B18 open correct.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3843.txt: May 16, 1923, 'The Alien Property Custodian may sell at private sale ... property of any nature whatsoever ... in parcels, lots or quantities for market value ... not exceeding Fifty Thousand Dollars ($50,000.) for each parcel', whenever he determines it necessary; and 'All Executive Orders heretofore issued are hereby amended and modified to conform to this order.' This is a standing general rule like EO 2832, not 'one disposition of named property' as the B18 basis states, and no single sale would exhaust it. Open is still right, but the stated route to decision (the Custodian's report of the sale) cannot decide it, and the gaps name only EO 2832 as a general rule.
correct_lead: open: standing general sale rule; ends only by revocation or supersession (or end of the Custodian's sale power), which must be searched for; not a single authorization

evidence: jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4354B.txt (OCR): Dec. 1925, Custodian authorized to sell on the New York Stock Exchange three stock holdings (American Can, American Car and Foundry, National Lead) of trust for Bernard Elkan 'in such lots, and at such times' as he sees fit. Several lots, no performance record; the one-end-per-lot gap is stated. B18 open correct.

jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_2958.txt: Sept. 13, 1918, 'I hereby declare the said sale to be void and of no effect, and I hereby authorize and direct the Alien Property Custodian to reject all bids' for the Helios cigar factory sale at Manila. jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_2845.txt: Apr. 24, 1918, private sale of 20 hogsheads of tobacco (Fallenstein) 'in one or more lots'. No performance record. B18 open correct; one-end-per-lot gap stated.

jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_3154.txt: Aug. 21, 1919, under sec. 4 of the Act of July 19, 1919, the CPI chairman shall 'relinquish and transfer to the Council of National Defense all papers ... and that upon such relinquishment and transfer the Committee on Public Information shall cease and be at an end'. Single act whose performance is not held. B21 open correct.
jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3150.txt: Aug. 16, 1919, private sale of Lot 77 in Square 159, Washington, D.C. (Jung). No performance record. B18 open correct.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3016H.txt: Polk order of Mar. 15, 1919 authorizing rejection of all bids (Frank Miller, $1,212,000) at the Feb. 1919 Bridgeport auction of International Textile stock, patents and trade-mark, and resale. Performance not held. B18 open correct.

jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_2837.txt: Apr. 11, 1918, revokes two licensing powers under EO 2729-A sections XI and XVII and adds 'no such license shall be granted until further order'. jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3180.txt (S20, held): 'I hereby rescind, as of the 14th day of July, 1919, the Executive Order of April 1[1], 1918', signed 25 November 1919. Interval 1919-07-14 to 1919-11-25 is right. The EO 2916 edge (Wikisource note) is a cross-reference; EO 2916 ratifies prior orders and does not end EO 2837.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4736A.txt: Oct. 5, 1927, Custodian authorized to sell at private sale 3,000 shares of Schutte & Koerting Co. preferred stock (Ernst Koerting estate) for $325,000. The lead says it was 'Revoked in full by Executive Order No. 6391, which names this order by number', dated 1931-01-10, under the open branch B18 and citing no held text of EO 6391. The held EO 6391 (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6391-code-fair-competition-for-the-mens-garter-suspender-and-belt.txt) is FDR's Nov. 4, 1933 approval of the NIRA code for the men's garter, suspender and belt industry; it does not mention EO 4736-A. held.py '4736' finds no other instrument. No ending basis exists.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3057.txt: Mar. 1919, 'I hereby designate and appoint Charles Arthur Richards as a member of the War Trade Board ... additional representative ... of the Food Administrator'. One appointment of one named person; B11 routes to PD-CS-ONE-PERSON (P4); War Trade Board candidate end (June 30, 1919, not held) disclosed.

jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4073A.txt (OCR): Sept. 1924, private sale for $53,333.34 of the Magnus interests in Cedar Rapids, Levy County (Fla.) and Cook County (Ill.) real estate. jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4224A.txt amends 4073-A to cover Cook County lots 25-27 'the sale authorized by said Order having contemplated the inclusion of this real estate'; this records no completed sale.
